body:
Upstream issue: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/39216
Mirror issue: https://github.com/amdpilot-org/sglang/issues/2585

## What changed

- Reproduced `asyncio.CancelledError` escaping from both `TokenizerManager._stream_one_response` disconnect polls.
- Added a narrow disconnect wrapper that treats receive-only cancellation as a disconnected client, allowing the existing per-request abort path to run.
- Preserved genuine handler-task cancellation by re-raising when the surrounding task is being cancelled.
- Added regressions for waiting and running requests plus connected and explicit-task-cancellation boundaries.
- Retained pre-fix/post-fix logs and a single-gfx950 real HTTP disconnect/health/follow-up probe under `reports/j-2c0ee86b22cc/`.

## Reproduce

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-2c0ee86b22cc/venv/bin/python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/managers/test_tokenizer_manager_rid_cleanup.py
```

The full module passes 30 tests and 3 subtests. The checked-in GPU probe can be rerun with the private deterministic fixture path documented in the report.

## Limitations

The original 4x NVIDIA RTX 6000D, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash weights, 200k-token request, TP=4 topology, and container image were unavailable. The real GPU check used one assigned AMD gfx950 and the qualified tiny random Llama fixture, so it validates transport and engine survival only, not DeepSeek semantics, long-context behavior, NVIDIA SM120, or distributed execution. No native code changed, so no native rebuild was applicable. The prepared interpreter did not include `ruff`; pytest and `git diff --check` were run.
